title: Charming Kids Mesh Jaal Mehndi Design for Back Hand
descriptionParagraphs: A traditional kids mehndi design tailored for the back of the hand, featuring dotwork and peacock motif. Rated as Medium, this pattern is perfect for an engagement.

Skin on the back of the hand is thinner than the palm, so the stain is usually lighter and fades sooner. Leaving the paste on for longer helps the colour develop. This pattern suits someone who is already comfortable with basic lines, dots and petals and wants to practise even spacing.
Children's mehndi uses small, simple motifs that can be finished in a few minutes. Children's skin is more sensitive than adults', so only natural henna paste should be used.
Application tips: Keeping the skin warm while the paste is on helps the colour develop. Pick a design that takes five to ten minutes; young children rarely sit still for longer.

image.alt: Kids Mesh Jaal mehndi design for back hand — charming henna pattern

faq.q: How long should I leave the mehndi paste on?
faq.a: Keep the paste on for at least four to six hours. Many people leave it overnight for a darker stain.

faq.q: Why does my mehndi look orange at first?
faq.a: Fresh henna stains are orange. The colour deepens to reddish brown over the next 24 to 48 hours as the dye oxidises.

faq.q: Is black henna safe?
faq.a: Natural henna is never black. Products sold as black henna often contain PPD, a hair-dye chemical that can cause skin reactions, so they are best avoided.

title: Detailed Kids Ring Pattern Mehndi Design for Front Hand
descriptionParagraphs: A contemporary kids mehndi design tailored for the palm, featuring bracelet cuff and crescent motif. Rated as Medium, this pattern is perfect for everyday.

The palm has the thickest skin on the hand, so henna stains darkest here. Keep the hand open and relaxed while the paste dries so the lines do not crack or smudge. This pattern suits someone who is already comfortable with basic lines, dots and petals and wants to practise even spacing.

Black henna often contains PPD, a hair-dye chemical that can cause serious skin reactions, and should never be used on children. Henna should not be used on babies, and children with G6PD deficiency should avoid it; ask a doctor if you are unsure.

Application tips: Leave the paste on for a shorter time, around one to two hours, and wash hands well afterwards. Do a patch test on the inner arm a day before, especially the first time a child wears mehndi.

faq.q: Is black henna safe?

faq.a: Leave the paste on longer, seal it with lemon and sugar, keep the skin warm, and avoid water for the first day after removing the paste.
